mainTopic: The ״מיין ושכר״ debate between רבי שמעון and the רבנן, and the rules of נזיר שמשון and נזיר עולם
overview: This amud finishes the argument between רבי שמעון and the רבנן about the words ״מיין ושכר יזיר״. The גמרא explains that the יין מצוה רבי שמעון forbids is wine a person swore to drink, following רבא's case of an oath to drink followed by נזירות. For the רבנן, the extra word ״ושכר״ teaches two rules. For רבי שמעון, ״שכר״ is used either for a גזירה שוה that forbids a כהן in the מקדש only wine, against רבי יהודה, or to teach that by נזיר one איסור does take effect on another. The גמרא then explains that the רבנן read ״מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין״ as teaching that the נזיר's grape איסורים combine. רבי שמעון does not need that rule, because for him any tiny amount gets מלקות. A new משנה teaches that saying "I am like שמשון," or describing him clearly, makes a person a נזיר שמשון, and the גמרא explains why each description is needed. A second משנה contrasts a נזיר עולם with a נזיר שמשון regarding cutting heavy hair and the קרבן טומאה. The גמרא says that משנה is missing a line and begins to restate it, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: מצוה wine cannot mean קידוש and הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that יין מצוה refers to the wine of קידוש and הבדלה, because a נזיר is already bound by his נזירות from סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is already sworn and bound about it from Mount סיני!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא had suggested that the ״מצוה wine״ רבי שמעון talks about is the wine of קידוש and הבדלה. Now it rejects that suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As explained here, a נזיר is bound by Torah law to keep the rules of נזירות, while drinking wine for קידוש or הבדלה is only a rabbinic matter. So it is obvious that he may not drink that wine, and no special פסוק is needed to teach it. The גמרא therefore has to find a different case of ״מצוה wine.״

keyTerms.meaning: Already sworn and bound from Mount סיני: a Torah obligation that rests on him
Wine that a person is obligated to drink
קידוש and הבדלה, the suggestion being rejected here

phrases.english: He is already sworn and bound about it
phrases.notes: This answers the suggestion just before this that ״מצוה wine״ means the wine of קידוש and הבדלה.

phrases.english: from Mount Sinai!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי מוּשְׁבָּע וְעוֹמֵד עָלָיו מֵהַר סִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made just before this section that יין מצוה means קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the identification of יין מצוה as קידוש and הבדלה. רבי שמעון's basic idea still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case a נזיר is obviously forbidden anyway, because his Torah-level נזירות outweighs a rabbinic obligation. A פסוק would be pointless.

steps.title: מצוה wine means wine he swore to drink
steps.stepSummary: Using רבא's case, the גמרא explains יין מצוה as wine a person swore to drink. If he later became a נזיר, the נזירות takes effect on what he swore about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like what רבא said: If someone said, "I swear that I will drink wine," and then said, "I am hereby a נזיר," the נזירות comes and takes effect on the subject of the oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of ״מצוה wine.״ It is wine that a person is required to drink because of an oath he made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he swears to drink wine, drinking it becomes a real obligation for him. Without a פסוק, we might think his later נזירות could not take effect on something he is already obligated to do. רבי שמעון's פסוק teaches that the נזירות does take effect, so he is forbidden to drink this wine too.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath that I will drink
I am hereby a נזיר: the standard words for accepting נזירות
Takes effect, lands on

phrases.english: Rather, it is like that which Rava said:
"An oath that I will drink [wine],"
and then he said: "I am hereby a nazirite" —
the naziriteship comes and takes effect on the oath.
phrases.notes: He means the נזירות takes effect on the wine he swore to drink, so now he may not drink it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation from step 1 with a workable case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the ״מצוה wine״ that רבי שמעון's פסוק forbids?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wine he swore to drink. His later נזירות takes effect on it anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that נזירות is strong enough to take effect even on something a person already obligated himself to do by an oath.

steps.title: The רבנן also need the פסוק for מצוה wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן: they too must forbid יין מצוה, so how can they use the פסוק for a different rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן too, don't they need this פסוק to forbid מצוה wine just like optional wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן and points out that they also hold that מצוה wine is forbidden. It asks where they learn that from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן used ״מיין ושכר״ to teach that one prohibition is enough to make someone a נזיר. But they also agree that a נזיר may not drink יין מצוה, and that rule needs a source too. It seems one פסוק cannot cover both rules.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, who disagree with רבי שמעון here
He needs it (the פסוק) for something else
Optional wine, drunk by choice and not as an obligation

phrases.english: And the Rabbis also,
isn't it needed by them
to forbid מצוה wine like optional wine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that יין מצוה has been defined, the גמרא asks how the רבנן derive that it is forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's use of ״מיין ושכר״ to teach that one prohibition is enough to make someone a נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן also need a source for forbidding יין מצוה. If the פסוק is used for that, nothing is left for their rule about accepting only one prohibition.

steps.title: The extra word ״ושכר״ teaches two rules
steps.stepSummary: The word ״ושכר״ is extra. That extra word lets the רבנן learn both rules from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have said only "from wine." Why add "and strong drink"? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the רבנן. The פסוק has an extra word, ״ושכר,״ so it teaches two rules instead of one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק were only about מצוה wine, ״מיין״ (from wine) would have been enough. Adding ״ושכר״ shows the פסוק has more to teach. So the רבנן learn both that יין מצוה is forbidden and that one prohibition is enough to make someone a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the פסוק say (it should have said)
Strong drink, an intoxicating drink
Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, ״מיין ושכר״ teaches two rules: יין מצוה is forbidden, and accepting one prohibition makes a person a full נזיר.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "from wine."
What is "and strong drink" for?
Learn two things from it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק (ריבוי) allows two separate teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One פסוק can teach only one rule, so the רבנן would have no source for one of their rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word ״ושכר״ lets the פסוק teach both rules.

steps.title: רבי שמעון uses ״שכר״ for a link to the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון cannot learn two rules from ״שכר,״ because he needs that word for a גזירה שוה with the כהנים in the מקדש. A כהן is forbidden only wine, not other intoxicating drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון would say: the reason the פסוק writes "strong drink" is to link "strong drink" here with "strong drink" said about the מקדש, as it is written: "Do not drink wine or strong drink, you and your sons with you." Just as for a נזיר only wine is forbidden and other drinks are not, so too for the מקדש only wine is forbidden, and other intoxicating drinks are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי שמעון does not accept the רבנן's "learn two things" answer. He needs the word ״שכר״ for a different teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״שכר״ appears both by נזיר and by the כהנים serving in the מקדש, and this matching word creates a גזירה שוה. By נזיר it is clear that ״שכר״ means a drink made from grapes, since only grape products are forbidden. So by the מקדש too, only wine is forbidden, and other intoxicating drinks are allowed. Because ״שכר״ is used up for this, it cannot teach the extra rule the רבנן learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach by comparison: to link two places with the same word (a גזירה שוה)
The Temple, here meaning the כהנים who enter it to serve
Regarding, in the case of
Intoxicating drinks other than wine

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון uses ״שכר״ for a גזירה שוה: just as a נזיר is forbidden only wine, a כהן serving in the מקדש is forbidden only wine and not other intoxicating drinks.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק by the מקדש says ״יין ושכר,״ which sounds like it forbids every intoxicating drink. The גזירה שוה teaches that, as with נזיר, ״שכר״ here also means only a grape drink.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon:
this is the reason the verse wrote "strong drink" —
to teach a link between "strong drink" here and "strong drink" said about the Temple.
As it is written: "Do not drink wine or strong drink,
you and your sons with you."

phrases.aramaic: מָה גַּבֵּי נָזִיר: יַיִן הוּא דְּלִיתְּסַר,
phrases.english: Just as with a nazirite, it is wine that is forbidden,
but other beverages are not,

phrases.aramaic: אַף גַּבֵּי מִקְדָּשׁ נָמֵי: יַיִן הוּא דְּלִיתְּסַר,
phrases.english: so too with the Temple, it is wine that is forbidden,
but other intoxicating beverages are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון does not learn two rules from ״ושכר״ the way the רבנן did in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is needed for another teaching (גזירה שוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ״ושכר״ seems extra, רבי שמעון should also learn two rules from it, as the רבנן do.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, ״שכר״ is used for the גזירה שוה with the מקדש, so it is not free to teach anything else.
steps.whyThisMatters: This also produces a practical הלכה: a כהן serving in the מקדש is forbidden only wine, not other intoxicating drinks.

steps.title: The גזירה שוה rules out רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה from step 5 teaches that a כהן is forbidden only wine. This rejects רבי יהודה, who says a כהן is liable even for foods like dried figs, honey, or milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes the view of רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: if a כהן ate a dried fig from קעילה, or drank honey or milk, and then entered the מקדש, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 5. It explains whose opinion the גזירה שוה is pushing away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that other things that can dull the mind also make a כהן liable when he enters the מקדש. רבי שמעון's גזירה שוה between ״שכר״ by נזיר and ״שכר״ by כהנים shows that only wine counts. That is why the word ״שכר״ is already used up for him.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to rule out
A dried fig from קעילה
The בית המקדש
Liable, deserves punishment

phrases.english: And this excludes the view of Rabbi Yehuda.
As it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If one ate a dried fig from Ke'ila,
or drank honey or milk,
and then entered the Temple, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 5's answer by naming the opinion that the גזירה שוה rejects.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the word is needed for a separate law, so it is not extra
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the גזירה שוה, one might follow רבי יהודה and forbid a כהן other dulling foods and drinks.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, ״שכר״ teaches that only wine is forbidden to a כהן, so the word cannot also teach a second נזיר rule.

steps.title: Second answer: רבי שמעון holds one איסור does not take effect on another
steps.stepSummary: Another reason ״שכר״ is used up for רבי שמעון: in general he holds that a new איסור cannot take effect on something that is already forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say a different answer: רבי שמעון does not hold that one איסור takes effect on another איסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different reason why רבי שמעון cannot learn two rules from ״שכר״. The next step brings the source for this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, for רבי שמעון, once something is already forbidden, a new איסור cannot be added on top of it. So he needs the word ״שכר״ to teach that by נזיר a second איסור does take effect. For example, if someone swore not to drink wine and then became a נזיר, both איסורים apply. That leaves ״שכר״ with no room for the רבנן's extra rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another answer
He does not hold of
A new prohibition taking effect on something already forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying that נזירות fails to take effect on wine that is already forbidden. Because רבי שמעון usually says an איסור does not take effect on another, a פסוק is needed to teach that by נזיר it does.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
Rabbi Shimon does not hold
that a prohibition takes effect on an existing prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the גזירה שוה reason of steps 5-6 with a different reason the word is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the word is needed for a separate law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think ״שכר״ is free for רבי שמעון to learn a second rule, as the רבנן do.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון needs ״שכר״ to teach that נזירות takes effect even on wine that is already forbidden, for example by an oath not to drink. This goes against his general rule that one איסור does not take effect on another.

steps.title: Proof: eating נבילה on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון's view: someone who eats נבילה on יום הכיפורים is exempt from the יום הכיפורים punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: one who eats נבילה on יום הכיפורים is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that רבי שמעון really holds that one איסור does not take effect on another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבילה is forbidden every day of the year. Because it is already forbidden, the איסור of eating on יום הכיפורים does not take effect on it for רבי שמעון. So he is exempt from the יום הכיפורים punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
The fast day when eating is forbidden
Exempt from punishment

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Shimon says:
One who eats a carcass on Yom Kippur
is exempt.
phrases.notes: He means exempt from the punishment for eating on יום הכיפורים, since the meat was already forbidden as נבילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 7 about רבי שמעון's general view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds איסור אינו חל על איסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about eating נבילה on יום הכיפורים

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with ״מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין״?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from ״מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין״ that one must accept all the נזיר איסורים. The רבנן also have this פסוק, so what do they learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: For the רבנן too, isn't it written: ״מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן and asks what they do with a פסוק that רבי שמעון uses for his own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads this פסוק to mean that a person becomes a נזיר only if he accepts every part of נזירות. The רבנן disagree with that rule, yet the פסוק is still in the תורה. So it must teach them something.

keyTerms.meaning: And for the רבנן too
Isn't it written?
Grapevine

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis too,
isn't it written:
"Anything that is made of the grapevine"!
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:4. This is the פסוק רבי שמעון uses to say a person must take on all the נזיר איסורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי שמעון's use of ״שכר״, the גמרא asks how the רבנן use the פסוק רבי שמעון relies on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק that רבי שמעון uses for his rule exists for the רבנן too, so it seems they would have to reach his rule.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches that the נזיר איסורים add up together
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that ״מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין״ teaches that the different grape איסורים of a נזיר combine together to make a full amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן would tell you: there, the פסוק teaches about the איסורים of a נזיר, that they combine with one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the רבנן use the פסוק for a different rule, the rule of combining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״מכל״, everything from the vine, show that all grape products count as one איסור for adding up. So small amounts of different grape products together make the full amount needed for punishment. This is why the רבנן do not have to learn רבי שמעון's rule from this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They would tell you
It taught
Combine, add up together

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: ״שכר״ is used up, either for the גזירה שוה with כהנים or to teach that נזירות takes effect even on wine that is already forbidden (איסור חל על איסור). ״מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין״ teaches that one must accept all of נזירות. רבנן: the same פסוק teaches that the נזיר's grape איסורים combine together.

phrases.english: The Rabbis would tell you:
There, it teaches about the prohibitions of a nazir
that they combine with one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9 by giving the פסוק a different meaning for the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a different meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק would seem to force the רבנן to agree that one must accept all the נזיר איסורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the רבנן, the פסוק teaches that the נזיר's grape איסורים combine together.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not need combining
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not use the פסוק for צירוף, because he does not need a rule that amounts combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון does not hold of combining.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי שמעון does not learn combining from the פסוק, as the רבנן did in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the רבנן used ״מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין״ to teach that the different grape foods add up to a full amount. רבי שמעון does not need that lesson, so the פסוק is free for his own teaching from step 9. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Combining: adding different forbidden foods together to reach the needed amount
He does not hold of it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon does not hold of combining,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון does not use the פסוק the way the רבנן do in step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the opposing view does not need the derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רבי שמעון also needs the פסוק to teach combining
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון holds there is no need for combining, so the פסוק teaches something else

steps.title: A ברייתא: any amount gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון holds even a tiny amount gets מלקות, and a כזית matters only for a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי שמעון says, any tiny amount is enough for מלקות. They only said a כזית for bringing a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי שמעון does not need combining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a tiny bit of forbidden food gets מלקות, there is no need for foods to add up to a כזית. A כזית is only needed for a קרבן, and a נזיר who eats grapes by mistake does not bring a חטאת. So for a נזיר, a rule about combining would teach nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even the smallest
Lashes given by בית דין
An olive-size amount, the usual amount for eating
An offering, such as a חטאת brought for a mistaken sin

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, even a tiny amount gets מלקות, so he does not need combining. That frees ״מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין״ for his own lesson.

phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
Any tiny amount is enough for lashes;
they only said an olive-size amount
with regard to bringing an offering.
phrases.notes: A נזיר does not bring an offering for eating grapes by mistake, so for him only the lashes matter.

steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון does not need צירוף
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון says כל שהו למכות

steps.title: The משנה of vowing to be like שמשון
steps.stepSummary: Someone who says he is like שמשון, or uses other descriptions of שמשון, becomes a נזיר שמשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says: I am like שמשון, like the son of מנוח, like the husband of דלילה, like the one who tore off the doors of עזה, like the one whose eyes the פלשתים gouged out, he is a נזיר שמשון.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists several ways of saying "I am like שמשון," and each one makes the person a נזיר שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person never says the word נזיר. Still, comparing himself to שמשון counts as a vow to be a נזיר like שמשון. What a נזיר שמשון must keep is explained in the next משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
I am hereby, the usual opening words of a vow
A special kind of נזיר modeled on שמשון
The Philistines, שמשון's enemies

steps.confusionAlert: A נזיר שמשון is not the same as a regular נזיר. He has his own special rules, which the next משנה explains.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: "I am hereby like Shimshon,"
"like the son of Manoach," "like the husband of Delilah,"
"like the one who tore off the doors of Aza,"
"like the one whose eyes the Philistines gouged out"
he is a nazir like Shimshon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comparing oneself to שמשון by name or by a clear description makes one a נזיר שמשון

steps.title: Why list so many descriptions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to list all these different descriptions of שמשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה need to teach all of these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists so many phrases. Saying "like שמשון" should have been enough. This question sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that the משנה looks repetitive. Every phrase points to the same person, so the extra ones seem unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A question about something that seems extra
To teach, meaning for the משנה to state it

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why do I need
to teach all of these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The long list of descriptions in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All the phrases mean the same person, so one should be enough

steps.title: "Like שמשון" alone could mean another person
steps.stepSummary: Saying only "like שמשון" might mean a different man named שמשון, so the משנה adds "like the son of מנוח."
steps.simpleTranslation: They are needed. If he only said "I am like שמשון," I would think he meant a different שמשון. So the משנה teaches "like the son of מנוח."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer: each description is needed. "Like שמשון" alone could mean some other man with that name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow only counts if it clearly points to the שמשון of תנ״ך. Adding "son of מנוח" narrows it to him.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed, meaning each case teaches something new
I would have thought, the first idea before the correction
It teaches us, the point the משנה is making

phrases.english: They are needed,
because if he said "I am hereby like Shimshon,"
I would think: he means a different Shimshon,
so it teaches us "like the son of Manoach."

steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Like שמשון" might refer to another man named שמשון
steps.terutzMaskana: "Like the son of מנוח" shows he means the שמשון of תנ״ך

steps.title: "Son of מנוח" could also be someone else
steps.stepSummary: Even "son of מנוח" might be the name of some other person, so the משנה adds descriptions only the real שמשון fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה only taught "like the son of מנוח," I would think there is someone else called that. So it teaches "like the husband of דלילה" and "like the one whose eyes the פלשתים gouged out."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. Even "son of מנוח" is not clear enough, so the משנה adds events that happened only to the real שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A name together with a father's name could still belong to someone else. A story-based description, like being דלילה's husband or blinded by the פלשתים, can only mean the שמשון of תנ״ך. That is why each description is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: There is someone who is called that
The husband of דלילה

steps.whatToRemember: Each description in the משנה is needed. Only a clear reference to the שמשון of תנ״ך makes a person a נזיר שמשון.

phrases.english: And if it taught "like the son of Manoach,"
I would think: there is someone who is called that,
phrases.notes: He means another man named שמשון whose father was also named מנוח.

phrases.english: so it teaches us "like the husband of Delilah"
and "like the one whose eyes the Philistines gouged out."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא from step 15 to the next descriptions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Son of מנוח" might be another person with that name
steps.terutzMaskana: Descriptions from שמשון's life clearly identify the שמשון of תנ״ך

steps.title: How a נזיר עולם differs from a נזיר שמשון
steps.stepSummary: The משנה compares a נזיר עולם and a נזיר שמשון in two areas: thinning heavy hair and the קרבן טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is the difference between a נזיר עולם and a נזיר שמשון? If a נזיר עולם's hair gets too heavy, he may thin it with a razor and then bring three animals as offerings. If he becomes טמא, he brings the קרבן טומאה. If a נזיר שמשון's hair gets too heavy, he may not thin it. If he becomes טמא, he does not bring a קרבן טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה sets two kinds of lifelong נזיר side by side and lists two differences between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds stay a נזיר forever. A נזיר עולם still follows the usual rules of a נזיר: he may cut some hair when it gets heavy, he brings the offerings, and he brings a קרבן טומאה if he becomes טמא. A נזיר שמשון follows his own special model, so he never cuts his hair and has no קרבן טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent נזיר, who stays a נזיר for his whole life
A נזיר modeled on שמשון: he never cuts his hair and has no קרבן טומאה
His hair grew heavy
He lightens it, meaning he thins the hair, with a razor
The offering a נזיר brings after becoming טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two. Both are lifelong, but only the נזיר עולם may thin his hair and bring a קרבן טומאה. The נזיר שמשון does neither.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מָה בֵּין נְזִיר עוֹלָם לְנָזִיר שִׁמְשׁוֹן?
phrases.english: MISHNA: What is the difference between a permanent nazir and a nazir like Shimshon?
A permanent nazir, if his hair grows heavy,
lightens it with a razor,
and brings three animals.
And if he becomes impure, he brings the offering for impurity.
A nazir like Shimshon, if his hair grows heavy,
does not lighten it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נִטְמָא — אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן טוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: and if he becomes impure, he does not bring the offering for impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מָה בֵּין נְזִיר עוֹלָם לְנָזִיר שִׁמְשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining how one becomes a נזיר שמשון, a new משנה contrasts him with a נזיר עולם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר עולם may thin heavy hair with a razor, brings three animals, and brings a קרבן טומאה. A נזיר שמשון may not thin his hair and brings no קרבן טומאה.

steps.title: Where did the משנה ever mention a נזיר עולם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה compares to a נזיר עולם without ever having introduced one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who mentioned a נזיר עולם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה talks about a נזיר עולם even though it never introduced him. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה introduced the נזיר שמשון, but it never said how one becomes a נזיר עולם. Comparing to something that was never introduced seems out of order, so the wording looks incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned its name? The משנה is talking about something it never brought up

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ נְזִיר עוֹלָם מַאן דְּכַר שְׁמֵיהּ?
phrases.english: GEMARA: A permanent nazir, who mentioned his name?
phrases.notes: In other words, the משנה never told us about a נזיר עולם, so how can it compare him to anyone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's comparison to a נזיר עולם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You cannot contrast two cases when one of them was never introduced in the משנה.

steps.title: The משנה is missing a line, which the גמרא supplies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing a line. It adds 'one who says I am a נזיר עולם is a נזיר' and then repeats the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something is missing from the משנה, and this is what it teaches: one who says 'I am hereby a נזיר עולם' is a נזיר. What is the difference between a נזיר עולם and a נזיר שמשון? If a נזיר עולם's hair gets too heavy, he may thin it with a razor and bring three animals. If he becomes טמא, he brings the קרבן טומאה. If a נזיר שמשון's hair gets too heavy, he may not thin it with a razor...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by saying a line is missing from the משנה. It adds that line, then reads the comparison again, and the comparison continues into the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the added line, the משנה first teaches that saying 'נזיר עולם' does make a person a נזיר. Only after that does it compare him to the נזיר שמשון. The comparison is repeated word for word, so the only new piece is the added opening line.

keyTerms.meaning: Something is missing: a line has to be added to the text of the משנה
And this is what it teaches
I am hereby, the opening word of a vow

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a standard tool of the גמרא. When a משנה seems to skip a step, the גמרא often says a line is missing and fills it in.

phrases.english: It is missing something
and this is what it teaches:
One who says, 'I am hereby a permanent nazir,'
phrases.notes: This is the line the גמרא adds. Everything after it repeats the משנה.

phrases.english: he is a nazir.

A permanent nazir, if his hair grows heavy,
lightens it with a razor and brings three animals,
and if he becomes impure, he brings the offering for impurity.
A nazir like Shimshon, if his hair grows heavy,
does not lighten it with a razor,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 by adding a missing line to the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to compare to a נזיר עולם that was never introduced.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה first teaches that saying 'הריני נזיר עולם' makes one a נזיר, and then it compares him to a נזיר שמשון.
